# Ezekiel 17 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** And-the-word-of YHWH came to-me, saying:

**2** "Son-of man, put-forth a-riddle and-speak a-parable to the-house-of Israel,

**3** and-say, 'Thus says the-Lord YHWH: The-eagle, the-great, great-of wings, long-of pinions, full-of feathers, which [had] embroidery, came to the-Lebanon, and-took the-top-of the-cedar.

**4** The-topmost-of its-young-twigs he-plucked, and-brought-it to a-land-of trade; in-a-city-of merchants he-set-it.

**5** And-he-took from-the-seed-of the-land and-put-it in-a-field-of seed; he-took-it by waters many — a-willow he-set-it.

**6** And-it-sprouted and-became a-vine spreading, low-of stature; to-turn its-branches toward-him and-its-roots under-him they-were; and-it-became a-vine and-made branches and-sent-out boughs.

**7** And-there-was an-eagle other, great, great-of wings and-abundant-of feathers; and-behold, this vine bent its-roots toward-him, and-its-branches it-sent toward-him, to-water-it from-the-beds-of its-planting.

**8** To a-field good, by waters many, it-was-planted, to-make branches and-to-bear fruit, to-be a-vine majestic.'

**9** "Say, 'Thus says the-Lord YHWH: Shall-it-prosper? Shall-he-not-pull-up its-roots and-strip-off its-fruit and-it-dry-up? All the-leaves-of its-sprout shall-wither.'"

**10** "Say, 'Thus says the-Lord YHWH: Shall-it-prosper? Shall-he-not-pull-up its-roots and-strip-off its-fruit and-it-dry-up? All the-leaves-of its-sprout shall-wither.'"

**11** "Say, 'Thus says the-Lord YHWH: Shall-it-prosper? Shall-he-not-pull-up its-roots and-strip-off its-fruit and-it-dry-up? All the-leaves-of its-sprout shall-wither.'"

**12** "Say, 'Thus says the-Lord YHWH: Shall-it-prosper? Shall-he-not-pull-up its-roots and-strip-off its-fruit and-it-dry-up? All the-leaves-of its-sprout shall-wither.'"

**13** "Say, 'Thus says the-Lord YHWH: Shall-it-prosper? Shall-he-not-pull-up its-roots and-strip-off its-fruit and-it-dry-up? All the-leaves-of its-sprout shall-wither.'"

**14** "Say, 'Thus says the-Lord YHWH: Shall-it-prosper? Shall-he-not-pull-up its-roots and-strip-off its-fruit and-it-dry-up? All the-leaves-of its-sprout shall-wither.'"

**15** "Say, 'Thus says the-Lord YHWH: Shall-it-prosper? Shall-he-not-pull-up its-roots and-strip-off its-fruit and-it-dry-up? All the-leaves-of its-sprout shall-wither.'"

**16** "'As-I-live,' declares the-Lord YHWH, 'surely in-the-place-of the-king who-made-him-king, whose oath he-despised and-whose covenant he-broke — with-him, in-the-midst-of Babylon, he-shall-die.

**17** And-not with-an-army great and-a-company vast shall-Pharaoh act for-him in-the-war, in-pouring-out a-siege-ramp and-building siege-walls, to-cut-off many souls.

**18** And-he-despised the-oath in-breaking the-covenant; and-behold, he-gave his-hand, and-all these he-did — he-shall-not-escape.'

**19** Therefore thus says the-Lord YHWH: 'My-oath which he-despised and-My-covenant which he-broke — I-will-bring-it upon his-head.'

**20** Therefore thus says the-Lord YHWH: 'My-oath which he-despised and-My-covenant which he-broke — I-will-bring-it upon his-head.'

**21** Therefore thus says the-Lord YHWH: 'My-oath which he-despised and-My-covenant which he-broke — I-will-bring-it upon his-head.'

**22** Thus says the-Lord YHWH: 'And-I-will-take I from-the-top-of the-cedar, the-high, and-I-will-set-it; from-the-topmost-of its-young-twigs a-tender-one I-will-pluck, and-I will-plant-it upon a-mountain high and-lofty.

**23** On-the-mountain-of the-height-of Israel I-will-plant-it, and-it-shall-bear branches and-produce fruit and-become a-cedar majestic; and-under-it shall-dwell every bird-of every wing — in-the-shade-of its-branches they-shall-dwell.

**24** And-all the-trees-of the-field shall-know that I, YHWH, have-brought-low the-tree high, have-exalted the-tree low, have-dried-up the-tree green, and-have-made-flourish the-tree dry. I, YHWH, have-spoken and-have-done.'"

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **17:3-4**: Ha-nesher ha-gadol — 'the great eagle.' The first eagle is Nebuchadnezzar; the cedar-top is King Jehoiachin, deported to Babylon in 597. The 'land of trade' is Babylon.

- **17:7**: The second eagle is Pharaoh of Egypt, toward whom Zedekiah (the vine) turns for military alliance, violating his vassal oath to Babylon.

- **17:22-24**: The messianic coda: YHWH Himself plants a tender shoot on Zion's mountain — a future Davidic king. The cosmic reversal (high/low, green/dry) signals eschatological restoration.

— EMET
